label: assumption
note: Tie-break priority stage (python -m tiebreak). Policy, not measurements: every value here is an assumption, shown as such in the UI. No weights: the keys are compared lexicographically, in this order.

threat_scenario.note: z in Mosca's inequality x + y > z: years from the plan's start to the EARLIEST Q-day scenario in config/assumptions.json (the most conservative choice).

internet_facing_kinds.note: Asset kinds treated as reachable from the internet (the 'edge' layer of config/atlas_web.json presentation).

patches.note: When a system uses both, ML-KEM comes first: traffic recorded today with classical key exchange can be read after Q-day (harvest now, decrypt later); a classical signature can only be forged by a quantum computer that exists at the time of the attack.
